_ghi_chu: EN-ALL GĐ 7–8 — bản phủ tiếng Anh của KB hoàng lịch (trang Hôm nay / Tuần này / Xem ngày tốt / lịch tháng / chọn ngày) — ban biên tập, chờ người bản xứ duyệt.

祭祀.nghia: ancestor offerings, death anniversaries, visiting pagodas and temples

祈福.nghia: praying for peace, health and good luck

开光.nghia: consecrating a newly brought-home statue or altar object

塑绘.nghia: sculpting or painting altar statues, painting altar pictures

齐醮.nghia: vegetarian ceremonies praying for peace or for the departed, at a pagoda or at home

斋醮.nghia: vegetarian ceremonies praying for peace or for the departed, at a pagoda or at home

沐浴.nghia: washing and cleansing before a ceremony

酬神.nghia: thanking the deities after a wish has come true

造庙.nghia: building or repairing communal houses, pagodas, shrines, clan halls

谢土.nghia: thanking the land after building or repair work is finished

出火.nghia: moving the stove or the altar to a temporary place

雕刻.nghia: carving, sculpture, engraving steles and signboards

嫁娶.nghia: weddings, fetching the bride, holding the wedding party

纳采.ten: First visit to the bride's family
纳采.nghia: the groom's family visits to raise the question, bringing first gifts

问名.nghia: the two families meet and exchange names, ages and birth dates

纳婿.nghia: a son-in-law coming to live with the bride's family

归宁.nghia: the bride visits her parents' home

安床.nghia: placing a new bed, setting the wedding bed, rearranging the bedroom

合帐.nghia: hanging curtains, laying bedding, decorating the newly-weds' room

订盟.nghia: two sides make a promise or agreement (often a marriage pledge)

进人口.nghia: adopting a child, taking a relative in to live with you, taking on household help

裁衣.nghia: cutting and sewing or buying new clothes (wedding outfits, New Year clothes)

挽面.nghia: facial threading, skin care, going to a spa

开容.nghia: grooming, make-up, hair and skin care

破土.nghia: digging a grave and building a tomb — not the same as breaking ground for a house

立碑.nghia: setting up or replacing a headstone

成服.nghia: putting on mourning clothes, announcing a death

除服.nghia: taking off mourning clothes at the end of mourning

开生坟.nghia: building a tomb in advance while the person is still alive
开生坟.ten_goc: Kai shengfen (building a tomb in life)

合寿木.nghia: making a coffin in advance for an elderly person

入殓.nghia: laying out the body and placing it in the coffin

普渡.nghia: food offerings for wandering souls (as at the full moon of the 7th lunar month)

入宅.nghia: moving in and living in a new home, the house-warming rite

安香.nghia: placing the incense bowl and the altar

修造.nghia: repairing, renovating and building the home

起基.nghia: digging foundations, driving piles, pouring the foundation

动土.nghia: starting construction, the ground-breaking rite for a house or a project

上梁.nghia: placing the ridge beam, pouring the concrete roof

竖柱.nghia: raising or pouring the house pillars

开井开池.nghia: drilling wells, digging ponds, building water tanks

作陂放水.nghia: building banks, letting water into fields, ponds and lakes

破屋.nghia: taking down an old house to rebuild

补垣.nghia: patching or rebuilding walls and fences

伐木做梁.nghia: felling trees, sawing timber, making beams and rafters for a house

作灶.nghia: building or installing a new stove

解除.nghia: tidying and cleaning the house, a cleansing rite

开柱眼.nghia: cutting joints, drilling holes in pillars and rafters

穿屏扇架.nghia: putting up partitions, fitting door and window frames
穿屏扇架.ten_goc: Chuan pingshan jia (fitting screens and frames)

盖屋合脊.nghia: roofing, pouring the roof, closing the ridge

开厕.nghia: building or repairing a toilet or septic tank

塞穴.nghia: sealing holes in walls, filling rat holes and ant nests, termite-proofing

平治道涂.nghia: levelling ground, building paths, pouring a yard, paving walkways

作厕.nghia: building or repairing a toilet or septic tank

筑堤.nghia: building dykes, shoring up pond and river banks

开池.nghia: digging a pond, making a fish pond or water tank

伐木.nghia: felling, cutting or pruning large trees

开渠.nghia: clearing ditches, digging drains and culverts

扫舍.nghia: sweeping and cleaning the whole house

合脊.nghia: finishing the roof ridge, pouring the roof

造畜稠.nghia: building pens for livestock, a home for pets

定磉.nghia: setting stone bases, pouring the pillar footings

修饰垣墙.nghia: painting, repairing and decorating walls and fences

架马.nghia: putting up scaffolding or temporary frames for building work

开市.nghia: opening a shop or office, starting to trade

挂匾.nghia: hanging a shop or company signboard

纳财.nghia: collecting money, receiving payment, stocking goods, recovering debts

求财.nghia: talking business, finding customers, looking for ways to earn

开仓.nghia: opening the stockroom and shipping goods for sale

买车.nghia: buying a car or other vehicle

置产.nghia: buying a house or land, acquiring major assets

出货财.nghia: delivering goods, paying out, large expenses
出货财.ten_goc: Chu huocai (sending out goods and money)

安机械.nghia: installing and test-running machines and equipment

造车器.nghia: making or assembling vehicles, machines, farm and trade tools

栽种.nghia: sowing seeds, planting trees and vegetables

结网.nghia: making nets and fishing gear, mending tackle

牧养.nghia: grazing and raising livestock and poultry

安碓磑.nghia: setting up a mortar or mill; today, installing milling and processing machines

习艺.nghia: learning a trade or a new skill

入学.nghia: the first day of school, starting a course

探病.nghia: visiting someone who is ill, visiting a hospital

见贵.nghia: meeting a superior, a partner or someone who can help you; going to an interview

乘船.nghia: travelling by train or boat, river and sea trips

针灸.luu_y: If you need to see a doctor, go now — do not wait for a good day; the almanac is only a custom for choosing dates for things that can be planned, and it is not medical advice.

出行.nghia: setting out on a long trip, business travel, holidays

移徙.nghia: moving house, moving to a new place or office

分居.nghia: splitting the household, moving out on your own

剃头.ten: A baby's first haircut, head shaving
剃头.nghia: shaving the head: a baby's first haircut, or shaving the head to become a monk or nun

整手足甲.nghia: trimming and tidying finger and toe nails, manicure

纳畜.nghia: buying or taking in livestock or pets

捕捉.nghia: getting rid of rats and pests, catching animals that got loose

教牛马.nghia: training cattle, dogs, cats and pets

赴任.nghia: the first day at work, taking up a post, transferring jobs

求医.nghia: starting a course of check-ups or treatment that can be planned ahead
求医.luu_y: If you need to see a doctor, go now — do not wait for a good day; the almanac is only a custom for choosing dates for things that can be planned, and it is not medical advice.

治病.nghia: starting a treatment or course of therapy
治病.luu_y: If you need to see a doctor, go now — do not wait for a good day; the almanac is only a custom for choosing dates for things that can be planned, and it is not medical advice.

词讼.luu_y: Legal deadlines do not wait for a good day; for a lawsuit, ask a lawyer.

立券交易.nghia: signing contracts, buying and selling, notarising

安机.nghia: installing and test-running machines and equipment

求医疗病.nghia: starting a course of check-ups or treatment that can be planned ahead
求医疗病.luu_y: If you need to see a doctor, go now — do not wait for a good day; the almanac is only a custom for choosing dates for things that can be planned, and it is not medical advice.

诸事不宜.nghia: the almanac advises not starting any major matter on this day

馀事勿取.nghia: the almanac advises doing only what is listed under Favourable and leaving everything else for another day

断蚁.ten: Getting rid of termites and ants
断蚁.nghia: spraying against termites, ants and woodworm

归岫.nghia: returning to your home town or old place

建.hop: travel, meeting people, starting something new

除.hop: cleaning up, medical treatment, clearing things away

满.hop: business matters, offerings, opening the stockroom
满.tranh: lawsuits, taking up a new post

定.hop: signing contracts, weddings, moving into a new home

执.hop: building and repairs, planting, starting to pursue a goal

危.hop: offerings, small tasks, work that needs care
危.tranh: climbing high, boat trips, risky ventures

成.hop: opening a business, weddings, starting school, signing contracts

开.hop: opening a business, starting school, weddings, travelling

闭.hop: building embankments, filling holes, finishing things
闭.tranh: opening a business, travelling, starting big ventures

dai_an.nghia: things go smoothly, safe journeys there and back

luu_lien.nghia: things tend to drag on and run late — prepare well

toc_hy.nghia: good news arrives fast, good for meeting people

xich_khau.nghia: arguments come easily — keep your words gentle

tieu_cat.nghia: a little luck, someone lends a hand

khong_vong.nghia: things tend to fall short — pick another time if you can

tam_nuong.nghia: the 3rd, 7th, 13th, 18th, 22nd and 27th of the lunar month — folk custom avoids weddings and openings

nguyet_ky.nghia: the 5th, 14th and 23rd of the lunar month — folk custom avoids long trips and big beginnings

duong_cong.nghia: 13 fixed days a year from an old book — folk custom avoids major undertakings

xung.nghia: a day that clashes with your zodiac sign — think twice about big matters or choose another day

tam_hop.nghia: a day in Three Harmony with your zodiac sign — good for work that needs joined effort

luc_hop.nghia: a day in Six Harmony with your zodiac sign — good for meeting people and making connections

hai.nghia: a day in Harm with your zodiac sign — keep the peace and avoid disputes

trung.nghia: a day that shares your zodiac sign — folk custom calls it your own day, keep a moderate pace

tue_pha.nghia: the day's branch clashes with the year's branch — popular date-selection books advise caution with big matters such as breaking ground or moving house
tue_pha.nguon: The Qing-dynasty almanac only treats the Year Breaker as a direction within the year; naming days after it is a habit of popular date-selection books.
tue_pha.luu_y: Only a label for your information; the system does not drop any day because of it.

thu_tu.nghia: a day set by the solar month in the old calendar — popular date-selection books often advise postponing celebrations and new beginnings
thu_tu.nguon: The Qing-dynasty almanac notes that the old calendar had this day and removed it from the main set of spirits; popular date-selection books still keep it.
thu_tu.luu_y: Only a label for your information; the system does not drop any day because of it.

天恩.nghia: kindness from above; good for acts of gratitude and praying for blessings

母仓.nghia: the mother storehouse; good for planting and raising animals

三合.nghia: joined strength; good for working together

月德.nghia: the month's star of blessing; good for kind deeds

月恩.nghia: the month's favour; good for happy occasions

天马.nghia: going far; good for setting out

驿马.nghia: movement; good for setting out and relocating

天喜.nghia: happiness; good for weddings and meetings

天医.nghia: the heavenly physician; traditionally linked with check-ups and treatment

天德.nghia: a great star of blessing; the almanac counts it a protected day

天赦.nghia: the day of pardon; the almanac ranks it among the very best days

白虎.nghia: a Black Path day; think twice about big matters

小耗.nghia: small losses; be careful with spending

劫煞.nghia: look after your belongings and take care on the road

月煞.nghia: the almanac advises postponing big matters

往亡.nghia: the almanac advises postponing long trips and taking up a new post

月破.nghia: the breaking day of the month; the almanac advises postponing big matters

大耗.nghia: losses; keep a firm hold on your money

归忌.nghia: the almanac advises postponing moving into a new home or coming back from a long trip

天刑.nghia: paperwork can get tangled; take care

朱雀.nghia: words can cause trouble; mind what you say

灾煞.nghia: stick to safe moves and avoid risks

天火.nghia: be careful with fire; postpone roofing

血忌.nghia: the almanac lists it as a day to avoid needles — medical care always follows your doctor's advice, never postponed because of the day

触水龙.ten: Touching the Water Dragon (Chu Shui Long)

四废.nghia: the almanac sees the day as low in energy; keep to small tasks

阴道冲阳.ten: Yin Path Clashing Yang (Yin Dao Chong Yang)

阴阳交破.ten: Yin and Yang Both Broken (Yin Yang Jiao Po)

阴阳俱错.ten: Yin and Yang Both in Error (Yin Yang Ju Cuo)

阴阳击冲.ten: Yin and Yang Striking (Yin Yang Ji Chong)

阳错阴冲.ten: Yang Error, Yin Clash (Yang Cuo Yin Chong)

四离.nghia: the day before an equinox or solstice; the almanac advises postponing big matters

阳破阴冲.ten: Yang Broken, Yin Clash (Yang Po Yin Chong)

banh_to.癸: Gui: do not go to court
banh_to.丑: Chou: do not hold capping rites
banh_to.寅: Yin: do not hold great sacrifices
banh_to.辰: Chen: do not weep and wail
banh_to.午: Wu: do not roof a house
banh_to.未: Wei: do not take unfamiliar medicine
banh_to.酉: You: do not entertain drinking guests
banh_to.戌: Xu: do not eat dog meat
